name: eventfd2
synopsis: int eventfd2(unsigned int initval, int flags);
description: eventfd2 creates a file descriptor for event notification, initializing a 64-bit counter with the specified initial value and applying the given flags. It allows user-space applications and the kernel to wait for and notify events.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags to modify behavior, such as EFD_CLOEXEC, EFD_NONBLOCK, or EFD_SEMAPHORE

return_value.success: Returns a new eventfd file descriptor
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: An unsupported value was specified in flags
The per-process limit on the number of open file descriptors has been reached
The system-wide limit on the total number of open files has been reached
Could not mount (internal) anonymous inode device
There was insufficient memory to create a new eventfd file descriptor

examples: efd = eventfd(0, 0);  // Note: This is from the man page example, adapted for eventfd2 context
switch (fork()) { case 0: /* Child process writes to efd */ }
